title: Theft
description: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, commits theft.
simpleExplanation: Theft means someone intentionally took movable property (such as a mobile phone, laptop, money, or vehicle) that belongs to you or was in your custody, without your permission.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years, or with fine, or with both. For petty theft value less than ₹5,000, community service can be ordered upon restitution.
cognizable: Cognizable (Police can register FIR and investigate without prior court warrant)
compoundable: Compoundable with permission of the court and consent of owner

title: Theft in dwelling house, means of transportation or place of worship
description: Whoever commits theft in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling, or used for the custody of property, or in any place of worship or public transport.
simpleExplanation: If property was stolen from inside your home, room, hostel, apartment, office, or vehicle, this aggravated section applies because the theft happened inside a private dwelling or protected premises.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 7 years, and shall also be liable to fine.

title: Cheating
description: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property.
simpleExplanation: Cheating applies when someone tricked or misled you into transferring money, giving away items, or entering into an agreement based on fraudulent promises or fake identities.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years, or with fine, or with both; if property transferred, up to 7 years.

title: Cheating by personation
description: A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is.
simpleExplanation: Applies when an impostor pretended to be a bank official, police officer, customer care representative, or someone you know to deceive you and take money or credentials.
punishment: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 5 years, or with fine, or with both.

title: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
description: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource, cheats by personation, shall be punished.
simpleExplanation: This is the primary cybercrime provision for online scams where criminals use phones, computers, fake apps, UPI links, or WhatsApp to pretend to be authorized entities and siphon your funds.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
compoundable: Compoundable with court permission under certain conditions

title: Punishment for identity theft
description: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished.
simpleExplanation: Applies when someone stole or misused your password, PIN, OTP, electronic signature, or biometric credentials without your authorization.
punishment: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 3 years and fine up to one lakh rupees.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
description: Whoever does any act with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person, and does thereby cause hurt to any person, is said voluntarily to cause hurt.
simpleExplanation: Applies when someone intentionally caused physical pain, disease, or bodily harm to you or another person (such as punching, slapping, or hitting).
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 1 year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.
cognizable: Non-cognizable (Cognizable if committed with dangerous weapons or on certain public servants)
compoundable: Compoundable by the person to whom hurt is caused

title: Criminal intimidation
description: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause alarm to that person.
simpleExplanation: Applies when someone threatened you with physical harm, death, property damage, or ruining your reputation to intimidate or force you into doing something against your will.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 2 years, or with fine, or with both; if threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, up to 7 years.

title: Criminal trespass
description: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property, or having lawfully entered into or upon such property, unlawfully remains there.
simpleExplanation: Applies when someone enters your land, plot, building, or room without right or permission, with an intent to occupy it, intimidate you, or commit an offence.
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
compoundable: Compoundable by the person in possession of the property trespassed upon

title: Deficiency in service
description: Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract.
simpleExplanation: Applies when a seller, service provider, repair company, courier, or telecom company failed to deliver what they promised, delivered damaged/defective items, or refused warranty service.
punishment: Civil remedy: Compensation for loss, refund of amount paid with interest, replacement of defective goods, and punitive damages.
cognizable: Adjudicated by District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

title: Information in cognizable cases (First Information Report - FIR)
description: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid, shall be signed by the person giving it. Information may also be given electronically (e-FIR).
simpleExplanation: This provision guarantees your right to give information regarding a serious (cognizable) crime to the police, obtain a free copy of the FIR, and permits electronic submission subject to verification.
punishment: Procedural mandate governing police officer duty; failure to record can invite disciplinary and legal action under Section 199 BNS.

title: Admissibility of electronic records
description: Any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be also a document, and shall be admissible in any proceedings, subject to certification regarding device operation.
simpleExplanation: Allows screenshots, CCTV footage, WhatsApp messages, emails, and bank PDF statements to be accepted as legal evidence in court, accompanied by a standard electronic record certificate.
